open_questions: High-cadence ground-based transits would test whether a repeatable 2.4 Rearth flat-bottomed transit (shape v_sigma=-3.075, fit_b=0.01556) exists at 11.7 d
Whether the deepest SPOC transits in sector 42 are spot-induced bumps mistaken for transits, which would explain the 0.0376 phase-curve ratio and 12083 ppm rotation amplitudes
dossier.public_summary: The dip changes depth dramatically from sector to sector and even from transit to transit, with odd and even events differing by 50 percent, a pattern inconsistent with a rock-steady planet transit. The closest nearby stars cannot explain it and imaging shows no clear on-target source, leaving the varying dips on the M dwarf itself most likely caused by spots and a few bad measurements. It is best rejected as a false transit rather than a planet.

reasons.why: All 7 transits are inconsistent in depth; the whole signal is carried by the few deepest events, not a repeatable planet depth.
Depth changes within the same TESS-SPOC light curve source, so it is not a calibration offset; sectors.p_constant=1.149e-13 indicates the dip strength is not stable.
